sections.vendors: Primark signed its first multi-year offtake agreement with a textile-to-textile recycler, Circ (announced 28 Sept). Circ will build a ~$500M plant at Saint-Avold, France, processing 70,000 tonnes of textile waste a year. Its process separates polycotton into recovered cellulose plus PTA/MEG for recycled polyester, with supply to Primark due to start in 2029. Volumes and financial terms weren't disclosed. No tier-1 supplier list or Open Supply Hub changes were reported this week.
sections.sustainability: The Circ deal backs Primark's aim to phase out conventional materials from its clothing by 2030. Primark says 39% of garments sold last financial year contained recycled fibres, up 32% year on year. Separately, Primark's 1 October breast cancer awareness range includes post-operative pieces and comes with a pledge of more than £1m to cancer charities across Europe and the US.
sections.strategy: International expansion continues through the Alshaya franchise. Bahrain (City Centre Bahrain) opened on 23 Sept, Qatar (Doha Festival City) opens on 29 Oct, and a second Qatar store and a new Kuwait store are planned for 2027. The 10 Sept trading update still frames the outlook: Q4 like-for-like sales down ~3% (UK/Ireland flat, Continental Europe down 4%), a £90m Sheffield fulfilment centre bought from Debenhams Group for future GB home delivery (no launch date yet), and the planned 2027 demerger from ABF under CEO Eoin Tonge.
sections.pricing: Primark is still running its 'Iconic Value' campaign: permanent cuts of up to 25% on hundreds of core lines across its 19 markets, carried through into Autumn/Winter. Examples: jeans at £9, cotton pyjamas from £7, men's hoodies from £9 and kidswear from £2, with stated improvements to fabric, fit and durability. Management says it will cut prices wherever a competitor undercuts it, which puts pressure on George, TU and F&F at entry price points.
sections.launches: On 1 October Primark launched a breast cancer awareness collection with post-operative products, backed by till donations in UK stores from 1 to 25 October. No major new licensed or designer collaboration was announced this week.
sections.gossip: Trade press still sees the Circ deal as a credibility test for next-generation recycling at scale, since supply only begins in 2029 and volumes are undisclosed. Analysts remain split on the demerger: Deutsche Bank's Adam Cochrane says enthusiasm will stay muted until like-for-like sales recover, and GlobalData warns a standalone Primark loses the cushion of ABF's food profits. Modaes describes the strategy as a 'return to basics' on price, with growth so far driven by new space rather than same-store sales.
soWhat: Recycled polyester demand is locking in. Circ supply starts in 2029, and the 2030 'no conventional materials' target means GRS-certified recycled polyester, recycled polycotton blends and traceability documentation will be expected of new Primark programmes. Mills should start qualifying recycled inputs now.

Iconic Value price cuts of up to 25%, made while promising better fabric and durability, will squeeze FOB costs on core basics (denim, jersey, fleece, nightwear). Prepare cost engineering options such as fabric weight, construction and yield changes before AW27 and SS27 costing rounds.

Growth is coming from new markets (GCC, US, Mexico) and from upcoming GB home delivery, not same-store sales. Expect more fragmented order flows, smaller replenishment drops and possible packaging and labelling changes for e-commerce. Suppliers with flexible MOQs and shorter lead times have an advantage.
